s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial weakness in a patient with a history of cancer treatment
salient_findings: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
Locally advanced, unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Received Folfirinox chemotherapy without significant response
Received gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel therapy
Developed bilateral facial drooping after 20 cycles of combined therapy and 16 additional cycles of nab-paclitaxel alone
Experienced grade 1 peripheral neuropathy which remained stable while taking vitamin B6 supplements
Developed severe edema due to capillary leak which led to discontinuation of gemcitabine
Neurological evaluation revealed bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
MRI Brain revealed bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis

shortlist.label: Leptomeningeal metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of cancer and neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of cancer and progressive facial weakness

shortlist.label: Geniculate ganglionitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral facial nerve enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral facial weakness and history of cancer treatment

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive facial weakness and history of recent chemotherapy

raw.rationale: Bilateral facial nerve enhancement on MRI Brain compatible with bilateral facial neuritis and bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness are consistent with geniculate ganglionitis, particularly in the context of the patient's history of chemotherapy and absence of other explanatory findings.

rejected.label: Leptomeningeal metastasis
rejected.why: MRI Brain showed no evidence of intracranial or leptomeningeal malignancy

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest brainstem involvement

rejected.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with varicella-zoster virus reactivation, which is not indicated in the vignette

rejected.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by ascending paralysis and areflexia, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of bilateral facial drooping and lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
